title: GPU Fault Modes: Enumeration & Shielding Protocol (early draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a short taxonomy of observable GPU fault modes we've seen across the fleet (ECC bursts, NVLink negotiation failures, driver hang patterns, and kernel panics), quick triage heuristics for on-call, and an initial "shielding" protocol to reduce noisy retries and avoid unsafe restarts. This is an early draft — operationally lightweight and intentionally prescriptive for nightshift engineers.

Executive summary:
- Recent months: recurring incidents where sustained ECC correctable-error rate spikes preceded driver hangs, then either graceful eviction or full kernel panic.
- NVLink negotiation glitches tend to correlate with multi-GPU workloads that reconfigure peers mid-job (model sharding, persistent KV cache).
- We need faster protective measures: (1) isolate affected NVLink fabric links, (2) throttle long-running batch jobs on nodes with rising ECC rates, (3) avoid automatic node-level reboot on first kernel OOPS.

Incident shorthand (example case): RDW-2029-06-03-epoch-breaker
- Signal: sudden drop in p99 generation throughput (4x latency tail) + hostd log: "GPU X: ECC correctable error surge"
- Metrics snapshot: ECC_correctable_rate[node-42] 1.2 -> 18 per hour over 20 minutes; NVLink_link_retries[slotA-B] increased from 0 to 42; coredumps: driver UVM stuck in timestack.
- Action taken (oncall): cordon node, stop new scheds, force-evict GPU processes, trigger diagnostic script (scripts/gpu-health/collect-dump.sh), escalated to hw-eng. Node reboot attempted -> kernel panic during early resume.

Primary hypotheses:
1) Progressive ECC accumulation (thermal + power droop) leading to state that surfaces as driver-side resource corruption.
2) NVLink transients amplify state inconsistency under multi-GPU synchronization, producing driver stack corruption.
3) Aggressive autoscaling/reallocations during heavy prefixes causing rapid link re-negotiation; driver regressions handle this poorly.

On-call quick heuristics (0-20 minutes)
- If ECC correctable rate > 10/hr AND NVLink retries rising: mark node as "degraded" and set scheduling weight to 0.
- If driver hangs but kernel still responsive: run uvm-service restart (if the node has >= 2 healthy GPUs) and monitor for repeated hangs; avoid full host reboot.
- If kernel panics observed in last 24h: quarantine host for hardware investigation, dump all telemetry and attach to SRE-3072.

Diagnostic commands (cheat-sheet)
- ecc counters: sudo nvml-tool --query ecc_counts --node node-42
- nvlink status: sudo nvidia-smi nvlink --monitor -i 0,1
- driver trace: journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "-30m" | tail -n 200
- kernel OOPS: /var/crash/* | grep -E "oops|panic" -A10
- quick cgroup kill: sudo cgdelete -g memory,cpu:/infer-alloc && systemctl restart infer-agent

Shielding protocol (v0.1) - automated responses we propose:
1) Deprioritize: autoscaler must reduce new allocations to node when ECC_correctable_rate > 5/hr for 15m, with backoff ramp.
2) Soft-isolate NVLink: If NVLink retries > 10 in 10m, mark the pair as "prefer CPU spill" — scheduler avoids multi-GPU placement affecting that fabric segment.
3) Slow-drain rather than immediate reboot: evict new jobs, attempt graceful uvm-driver restart twice (sleep 60s between). Only escalate to host reboot if kernel OOPS or unresolved hangs after restart attempts.
4) Blacklist firmware: when a node triggers same firmware stack trace twice in 7 days, add to temporary firmware-blacklist and schedule maintenance.

Runbook (oncall flow) - concise steps:
1) Alert received (ECC spike / driver hang / kernel panic).
2) Evaluate severity: (a) ECC spike without hangs -> apply "Deprioritize" policy; (b) driver hang -> attempt uvm restart; (c) kernel panic -> quarantine and collect core + hw logs.
3) Collect artifacts: (list above) + strace of top inference process if alive, nvtop screenshot, system power/thermal counters. Upload to SRE ticket.
4) Escalate to hw-eng for suspected board-level defects. If multiple nodes in same rack report NVLink faults, involve network/hw owner.

Open questions & risks:
- Will isolating NVLink pairs cause unfair capacity fragmentation and more scheduling churn? Need simulation.
- Potential for false positives in ECC counters due to sampling intervals. Adjust thresholds after 2-week burn-in.
- Driver restart might leak memory; require post-restart health checks (agent memory, python worker counts).

Planned follow-ups (owners):
- Miguel: build simulator to model capacity impact of NVLink soft-isolation (due 2029-06-20).
- Akira: implement a lightweight ECC-rate alert rule in metrics pipeline with 1m resolution (2029-06-14).
- Sofia: prototype scheduler flag to avoid co-scheduling on affected fabric pairs (PR draft, infra repo) (2029-06-18).
- Lena (me): coordinate postmortem template and consolidate artifacts for SRE-3072; propose adjustments after 2-week observational window.

Notes to self (nightshift):
- Keep "avoid-host-reboot" mantra. Reboots are last-resort; they repeatedly made reproduction harder for hw-eng.
- When collecting dmesg, always copy /sys/devices/system/node/ to the artifact bundle; rare but helpful.
- If you see the string "nvlink: retry limit reached" search for prior firmware updates in the node's image history.

Appendix: quick log excerpt (redacted)
[2029-06-03T03:15:07Z] node-42 nvlink: slotA-slotB retry count 27
[2029-06-03T03:16:11Z] node-42 kernel: NVRM: RmMapIb failed, reason 3
[2029-06-03T03:16:49Z] node-42 driver: uvm: thread stuck in uvm_kthread_fault_handler
[2029-06-03T03:18:02Z] node-42 kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing: GPU UVM state corrupted

This file will be iterated; please add examples of false-positive incidents and any counter-examples where the node recovered after uvm restart (helps tune thresholds).
